Schedule baseline benchmark run (Redwood hosted) week of 2027-11-08
Set up VPC peering test for Private deployment with infra team - target 2027-11-12

Timeline & gating criteria for expanding POC
transcript:
Header: 2027-11-02 16:00 UTC | Duration: 48m | Attendees: Samir Patel, Lina Cho (Redwood); Michael Reeves, Sara Kim, Tom Alvarez, Priya Nair (Nova)

[00:00] Samir: hey everyone, thanks for joining, can you hear me ok?
[00:04] Michael: yep, loud and clear. thanks, Samir.
[00:06] Samir: cool, quick agenda, Lina and I will run through the POC scope, then dig into workload numbers - qps, concurrency, token profiles - and agree on benchmarks and timeline.
[00:15] Sara: sounds good. our main ask is that p95 latency for interactive flows stays under ~300ms and we can hit our throughput targets without crazy cost.
[00:23] Lina: understood; we'll try to map that to concrete qps and concurrency, and propose a benchmark matrix.
[00:29] Tom: just to add, our traffic has a small number of very large prompts - like 2k tokens - but most are short, 50-150 tokens. there is a heavy tail.
[00:38] Lina: ok heavy-tail is important. do you have a histogram or average numbers?
[00:42] Tom: we can pull distribution - ballpark now: median input ~120 tokens, 90th ~600, 99th ~1800. output generally smaller, median ~60, 95th ~300.
[00:54] Samir: perfect. that helps. question on qps - what's the steady-state and peak you see?
[01:01] Michael: steady-state user-facing calls are about 8 qps globally for main product. during batch jobs and end-of-day things we spike to 60-70 qps for short windows, but concurrent user-facing sessions can reach 30-40.
[01:12] Lina: so for POC we'll want to test for steady 10 qps, spikes to 70 qps, and concurrency up to 40. does that align?
[01:20] Sara: yes, but for the interactive flows we care about p95 at concurrency 20-30. batch can be higher latency.
[01:27] Priya: on security, we need to validate VPC options and key management - KMS/HSM - and that logs/audit are available. also data residency concerns for EU traffic.
[01:36] Samir: we'll include Redwood Private options in the pack; we support customer-managed KMS and audit logging. Lina will share specific docs.
[01:41] Lina: yep, I'll include the VPC checklist and the infra runbook.
[01:44] Michael: good. on success criteria, here's what we want to see: p95 < 300ms for interactive endpoints at concurrency 20, no more than 3% error rate, and cost per 1M tokens within ~30% of your estimate. also must pass baseline security checks.
[01:57] Samir: makes sense. we'll propose a short list of tests: baseline latency/throughput on your sample prompts, stress test for spikes, and regression checks on quality with a small eval set.
[02:08] Tom: for tokens, remember outputs are sometimes larger when model is generating context expansions - want to make sure caching helps.
[02:14] Lina: yes, we can test prefix/KV cache effects. for the POC we'll run three modes: hosted Redwood API, Redwood Dedicated (reserved), and Redwood Private VPC to compare latencies and costs.
[02:26] Michael: timeline? we need results before end of November to decide on annual budget.
[02:31] Samir: ok target: start intake this week, benchmark runs week of Nov 8, analysis by Nov 12-15, and decision meeting Nov 18.
[02:40] Sara: tight but doable.

[10:05] Lina: diving into workload modeling - we typically convert your qps/concurrency into required GPU footprint. with your median/90/99 token numbers and target latency, rough starting point is 1x A100-equivalent per ~50 concurrent interactive sessions depending on model and quantization.
[10:22] Tom: we plan to use an open LLM baseline, around 18B dense.
[10:27] Lina: good note. 18B will have higher KV and memory needs. quantized 4-bit runtimes change throughput; we'll include model variants (18B dense, 18B int4, 7B) in the benchmark matrix.
[10:38] Michael: any estimate for cost delta between hosted and private?
[10:41] Samir: rough thumb - hosted usually higher per-token but lower ops overhead; private/dedicated has lower unit cost at scale but needs committed capacity. we'll provide concrete numbers in the POC pricing.

[20:00] Tom: for traffic shape, our peak bursts are short - 30-90s - and often many small requests arrive in parallel (concurrency bump). we care about cold-starts and KV warmups too.
[20:12] Lina: we'll include tests for cold vs warm cache with synthetic traffic that simulates your burst patterns. also continuous batching behavior matters for throughput/latency tradeoff; we'll measure token-per-second and per-request latency at different batching windows.
[20:26] Michael: what's your suggested benchmark harness?
[20:29] Lina: we'll take your 1k prompts, split into interactive (60%) and batch (40%), derive sample rate to hit steady 10 qps for 30 minutes, then run spike tests 0->70 qps ramp in 60s, and concurrency stress at 40 concurrent for 5 minutes. repeat across model variants.
[20:45] Samir: and we'll record p50/p95/p99, cost estimate, failure rate, and token throughput.

[30:10] Priya: quick note on compliance — please include data retention options and ability to disable logging for PII flows.
[30:18] Samir: yes, Redwood supports configurable retention and ability to exclude certain routes from logs; we'll include that in the security pack.

[35:00] Michael: one more question: does Redwood provide any built-in traffic modeling tools or will we need to script our own load generator?
[35:07] Lina: we have an internal harness we can share templates for; it's not a SaaS offering but we'd provide the scripts and configs and can run initial hosted runs ourselves. for private runs we can hand you the harness.
[35:18] Tom: good — that saves time. can we get latency breakdown per token and per stage (network, kv lookup, kernel execution)?
[35:26] Lina: yes we'll include tracing hooks and per-token cost/latency breakdown in the console for the benchmark.

[42:00] Samir: recap of agreed points and next steps: Redwood sends POC SOW and pricing, security docs, and benchmark harness by Nov 4; Nova provides sample prompts and priority flows by Nov 5; baseline runs week of Nov 8 with results midweek; decision meeting Nov 18.
[42:20] Michael: that's right. thanks all.
[42:24] Sara: thanks, appreciate the quick turnaround.
[42:26] Samir: thanks everyone; we'll follow up with calendar invites and the artifacts.

End of transcript.
